newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Mannesmann sees level 1997 telecom profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mannesmann sees level 1997 telecom profit.

text.p: German engineering group Mannesmann AG said on Tuesday high investments in fixed-line and mobile phone networks would result in flat 1997 returns in its profitable telecommunications arm.

Because of investments needed to build up its Mannesmann Arcor network and expand its D2 mobile system, there would be "no increase" in telecommunications results this year, managing board member Klaus Esser said at a news conference.
But Mannesmann's group profits were still exepcted to rise, even though telecoms has generated almost all of the company's profit in the last few years, stock analysts said.

"Through improvements in other business areas, profit will increase overall," said Richard Schramm, who follows Mannesmann at Trinkhaus Capital Management GmbH. "There is no problem. In 1998, there should be a positive growth rate in the telecommunications profits."
Rolf Doerfler at WestCapital said the dollar's strength and improvement in the German economy were boosting Mannesmann's industrial units, helping to offset the flattening of telecom results.
"I think profit will still increase in 1997, but not as strongly as the year before," he told Reuters.
Schramm added he saw no reason to change his forecast of net income rising 16 percent to 700 million marks and sales increasing 10 percent to 35 billion marks in 1997.
Last year telecommunications generated 947 million marks of Mannesmann's 1.01 billion marks in profit on ordinary activities.
In the first quarter, Mannesmann saw group sales rise 14 percent to 8.2 billion marks and orders increase 13 percent to 10.2 billion marks, chief executive Joachim Funk said on Monday.

Its tubes and trading business and automotive technology unit both showed "clear growth", with first-quarter orders rising 22 percent and 15 percent, respectively, Funk said without providing further details.

Tubes and trading, which was put into a steel pipe venture with French steel maker Vallourec SA in February, was profitable in the first quarter, after years of losses. Engineering orders slipped one percent, hurt by seasonal factors, Funk said.

Telecommunications sales in the quarter soared 69 percent to 1.4 billion marks, with D2 mobile revenue rising 42 percent, he said. Arcor, a venture formed last summer with the telecom network of German railroad Deutsche Bahn AG, had first-quarter sales of 200 million marks, he said.

Mannesmann planned to invest nine billion marks in telecommunications businesses over the next five years, much of it going toward making Arcor competitive with the former monopoly phone company Deutsche Telekom AG, Funk said.
Start-up costs would cause Arcor to lose about 300 million marks this year, Esser said. Arcor lost 100 million marks in 1996.
The company would also invest heavily to expand D2, Germany's largest mobile net after Telekom's T-Mobil service, and in a venture with Cegetel, the number two phone company in France, Funk said.
Mannesmann shares closed floor trading on Monday up 8.50 marks at 651.
